client.node: 22.22.2, the server's runtime; the client is a native binary
client.model: The client's default model on this account, not pinned
client.provider: Anthropic API, reached from the container

settings.discovery_mode: Deferred: all 133 names listed at start, each schema loaded through ToolSearch before a call

tester: A Claude Code agent session run for the repository owner, headless

C01.notes: Connected on a cold start and listed all 133 tools with the expected hash, by default and with MCP_PROTOCOL_NEGOTIATION=auto; both opened with a server/discover probe at 2026-07-28. The catalog script agrees in both eras with no TestRail request. Neither credential appears in a client transcript or in any line the server wrote to stdout or stderr.

C02.notes: In a session that called no TestRail tool, seven ToolSearch select: queries returned all 133 tool references; the returned names hash to the expected catalog hash. A probe session shows the deferral: the model loaded a schema before calling the tool.

C03.notes: All 28 tasks chose the intended tool first, with valid arguments and no tool error. 26 match the corpus arguments exactly; get_shared_steps added an explicit page mode, and get_roles asked for all roles. Ten sessions made follow-up calls, listed in the evidence: next pages, or reads that checked the stand-in's canned replies. None was a retry after an error.

C04.notes: A get_cases page reached the model whole, about 18.6 KB, with its IDs, custom field, page boundary and continuation. For get_roles, which has no manual continuation, the model read manual_continuation false and next_action all, and did not try the raw link.

C05.notes: A complete read returned 150 cases with complete true. The host moved the 55 KB result to a file; the model read its start and end and took the count from returned. Two other sessions of this read ran out of turns. Project 990045 stopped with PAGINATION_LIMIT, reason max_duration, after 3 pages and 45 seconds, with no partial data.

C06.notes: An unknown argument reached the server, got INVALID_ARGUMENT, and sent no TestRail request. Drift returned the data with a SCHEMA_DRIFT warning; an unusable reply returned INVALID_RESPONSE with no data. When the model wrote malformed JSON, the client refused it before the server.

C07.notes: Create, update, bulk update, close and delete each used their own tool, schema and annotations, and each reached TestRail once. A 400 and a 500 both returned UPSTREAM_ERROR with write_outcome unknown, told apart by http_status. Neither host nor adapter retried.

C08.notes: An upload inside the root succeeded; one outside it got FILE_ACCESS_DENIED with not_started and sent nothing. Repeated downloads wrote distinct 19-byte files that survived a restart. A 404 and a timed-out download left no file.

C09.notes: A 717 KB page arrived whole in a file the host saved. With jq allowed, jq parsed the whole file and the model recovered the count, first and last IDs and pagination; that page had no warnings and no continuation. A 3 MB page returned RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE; the same list with all returned PAGINATION_LIMIT, reason max_bytes, with no partial data.

C10.notes: Five parallel calls to a 20-second reply: the fifth got BUSY at once with no request, and the four admitted ones shared one driver request and timed out together at 15 seconds with TIMEOUT. After the replies settled, an ordinary call was admitted again. An interrupt sent through the SDK input channel reached the server as notifications/cancelled; it recorded CANCELLED and the stand-in logged the request as abandoned. The aggregate budget is in C05.

C11.notes: 50 headless sessions each started the server cold and saw the same 133-tool catalog. 53 of 55 server processes stopped cleanly with exit code 0; the host ended the two interrupted C10 sessions before the drain finished. No process remained. Only cold restarts were exercised, not a reconnect within a session.

C12.notes: With the reference filesystem server connected too, TestRail still listed 133 tools beside its 14, with no name collision, and calls to both servers worked.

limitations: Fixture stand-in only. No live TestRail was contacted, and the stand-in's canned replies do not echo the IDs asked for.
Headless sessions only (claude -p, with --max-turns per session). The interactive /mcp view and the approval prompts were not exercised.

Results over 25,000 tokens are moved to a file. The server's result is one line of JSON, which the Read tool cannot page. In headless mode tail and grep ran without approval, while jq and python3 needed it; the full 717 KB page was recovered once jq was allowed. A raised MAX_MCP_OUTPUT_TOKENS did not bring a 54 KB result back inline.
The server ran under a recorder that passes stdio through unchanged, to read the negotiated revision, rather than being started directly.
The package is the development version, not a release.
The model is deliberately not named in this record, a departure from the guide's rule, so the C03 selections and the C05 and C09 behaviour are tied to an unpinned default model.
One Linux container only; macOS and Windows were not tested.
The driver coalesces identical in-flight reads: the four admitted reads of one ID in C10 shared one request.
